title: BECE National Values Education: Security Education - National Values Education - Observing and Reporting Common Crimes
exam: BECE National Values Education: Security Education
subject: National Values Education

questions.q: Effectively observing common crimes in one's neighbourhood requires a citizen to be:
options: Heavily armed at all times
Highly vigilant and security conscious
Hostile to strangers
Indifferent to community affairs
questions.explain: **Vigilance** and security consciousness allow individuals to notice suspicious movements or activities without unnecessarily putting themselves in danger.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Security Education
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: If a citizen witnesses an armed robbery taking place, what is the most appropriate response?
options: Confront the armed robbers immediately
Run toward the scene to take close-up photographs for social media
Retreat to a safe distance and secretly call the police or emergency lines
Shout loudly to alert the robbers of their presence
questions.explain: The most **appropriate response** is to ensure personal safety first and then contact law enforcement (the police) so trained professionals can handle the armed threat.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Security Education
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: Why do some citizens hesitate or fail to report common crimes to the appropriate security agents?
options: Fear of victimization and lack of trust in the system
They are mandated by law to mind their own business
They enjoy seeing crimes being committed in their neighbourhood
Because the police command citizens not to report crimes
questions.explain: A major challenge in observing and reporting crimes is the **fear of reprisal (victimization)** by the criminals, coupled with a lack of confidence in the confidentiality of law enforcement.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Security Education
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: When a suspect is caught stealing in a market, the correct legal procedure is to:
options: Beat the suspect to serve as a warning to others
Hand the suspect over to the police for investigation and prosecution
Force the suspect to pay double the price of the stolen item
Strip the suspect naked and parade them round the market
questions.explain: Taking the law into one's own hands (jungle justice) is a crime. The only appropriate and legal response is to **hand the suspect over to the police**.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Security Education
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: Which of the following represents an inappropriate response to emergency crime situations?
options: Calling the police emergency toll-free numbers
Providing useful descriptions of suspects to authorities
Taking the law into one's own hands to dispense immediate justice
Testifying truthfully in a court of law
questions.explain: **Taking the law into one's own hands** (jungle justice or vigilantism) bypasses the judicial system, denies the suspect a fair trial, and often leads to the death of innocent people.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Security Education
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: To effectively report a crime, an observer should ideally take note of all the following details **EXCEPT**:
options: The physical description of the perpetrators
The time and exact location of the incident
The political party affiliation of the victim
The escape route or vehicle used by the criminals
questions.explain: When reporting a crime, details like physical descriptions, time, location, and escape routes are crucial for investigation. The **political affiliation** of the victim is irrelevant to the criminal investigation.
